div.head: Rect 20, 20.1, 20.2
div.ab: [20] Hæigwerde gebyreð, þæt man his geswinces lean gecnawe on ðam endum, ðe to etenlæse licgan; forðam he mæig wenan, gyf he þæt ær forgymð, þæt him man . . . [20.1] … hwilces landsticces geann, þæt sceal beon mid folcrihte nyhst etenlæse; forðam gyf he for slæwðe his hlafordes forgymð, ne bið his agnum wel geborgen, gif hit bið ðus funden. [20.2] Gyf he ðonne eal wel gefriðað, he healdan sceal, ðonne bið he godes leanes ful wel wyrðe.

[20] Heiwardo pertinet, ut merces laboris eius compensetur in eam partem segetis, que pascuis ádiacet; quia scire debet, si minus hoc seruabit, dampnum segetis imputabitur illi. [20.1] Et si aliqua terrę portiuncula permittatur ei, secundum ius publicum debet esse uicina compascuis, ut, si per desidiam eius seges infestabitur, a suo primitus expetetur.

Hæigwerde gebyreð þæt man his geswinces lean gecnawe on ðam en|dum ðe to etenlæse licgan forðam he mæig || wenan gyf he þæt ær forgymð þæt him man hwil|ces landsticces geann þæt sceal beon mid folc|rihte nyhst etenlæse forðam gyf he for slæwðe his hlafordes forgymð ne bið his ag|num wel geborgen gif hit bið ðus funden . gyf he ðonne eal wel gefriðað he healdan sceal ðonne bið he godes leanes ful wel wyrðe .

To the hedge-warden it is fitting that one knows that his labour’s reward [be] on the [field] ends which lie [closest] to the common pasture; because he can expect that if he first neglects that, that one [will hold] him [responsible] for whatsoever damage to the land. That [land which] is granted [to him] should be, by folk-custom, nearest to the common pasture, because if he should neglect his lord’s [land] out of laziness, [then] his own [land] will not be well-protected [either], if it is located thus. If, when all that he must tend is well-looked after, then he is fully well-worth a good reward.

[20] Dem Gehegewart gebührt, dass seiner Mühe Lohn anerkannt [entgolten durch Äcker neben dem Weideland, die eindringendes Vieh zuerst gefährdet] werde an dén Enden, die an der Weide liegen; denn er darf erwarten, wenn er dies nicht erst schützt, dass man [die Herrschaft] ihm (den Flurschaden zur Last legen wird. [20.1] Also wenn man [die Herrschaft] ihm fehlt B) ein Stück Land gewährt, soll dies gemeinrechtlich nächst der Weide liegen; denn wenn er aus Trägheit nicht seines Gutsherrn achtet, ist er für sein Eigen nicht sicher geborgen, wenn es [sein Land neben der Weide angewiesen worden ist], wie besagt, befunden worden ist. [20.2] Wenn er dagegen alles wohl schützt, was er hüten soll, dann ist er recht wohl guter Belohnung werth.

[20] To the hayward is due that the reward of his labour be recognised [paid by acres next to the pasture, which straying cattle first endanger] at those ends [of the fields] that lie beside the pasture; for he may expect, if he does not first protect this, that [the lord] (will lay the damage to the crops at his door. [20.1] So if [the lord] — lacking in B) grants him a piece of land, it shall by common law lie next to the pasture; for if through sloth he neglects his lord's [interest], his own is not safely protected, if it is found [assigned next to the pasture] as said. [20.2] If, on the other hand, he protects well everything he should guard, then he is fully worthy of a good reward.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 20–20.2. B skips a line here, according to the Quadripartitus (ending, like the previous line, with ‘him man’); the archetype began 20.1 with ‘⁊ gif him man’; Liebermann supplies the sense from the Quadripartitus (printed in bold). In 20.2 the omission of the relative pronoun (‘he healdan sceal’) was still rare then; or the original read ‘-ðað þæt’. The Quadripartitus lacks 20.2. K: spacing corrected.
